text: dsh-split-screen 是面向 DSH Web 的多会话分屏工作区，可在同一页面并排查看多个 agent 对话。它通过 Web 客户端覆盖层承载递归的横向或纵向面板，并复用 DSH 原生会话、消息和输入组件。用户可从侧栏拖入会话、拖动分隔线调整布局、切换焦点、关闭面板，也可在完整输入框与紧凑输入行之间切换。适合需要同时跟进多个 DSH 会话的用户；布局保存在本地浏览器存储中，无需额外 API 密钥。

dsh-split-screen adds resizable panes to the DSH web client so users can view several agent conversations at once. Drag sessions from the sidebar, move between panes, and switch between full and compact composers. It reuses native conversation components and stores layouts in browser storage.
我想在一个窗口里同时看几个 DSH 对话。
能不能把多个 agent 会话并排放在一起？
想把侧边栏里的会话拖进分屏工作区。
怎样调整不同聊天面板的大小和方向？
我需要快速切换正在查看的会话面板。
有没有办法在窄面板里用更紧凑的输入框？
I want to follow several DSH conversations side by side.
Can I split the web workspace into panes for different agent sessions?
dsh-split-screen 的功能「拖放会话分屏」：从会话侧栏拖入对话，并在面板边缘放下以创建横向或纵向分屏；放在中央可移动或交换会话。
dsh-split-screen 的功能「并排会话面板」：工作区为每个面板绑定独立会话，并承载原生对话内容，便于在一个 Web 页面同时查看多个 agent 会话。
dsh-split-screen 的功能「紧凑输入切换」：在聚焦面板按 Alt+T 可切换完整输入框与紧凑单行输入；面板较矮时会自动采用紧凑模式。
dsh-split-screen 的功能「面板焦点快捷键」：使用 Alt+Shift 加方向键将键盘焦点移到相邻面板，便于在多个会话之间导航。

Split-screen workspace for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI — chat with several
agents side by side, in panes that look and behave exactly like the stock
DeepSeek conversation.

dsh-split-screen README · What's new in 1.7.0：- **Programmatic navigation now follows the split.** `Alt+↑/↓` / `Alt+1‑9` from
  dsh-session-hotkeys, the stock **New Session** button, agent-team / IM /
  notification opens and any other `uiWorkspace.openSession()` caller move the
  root session binding and the focused pane with it — exactly like a sidebar
  click — instead of silently changing the covered stock view behind the
  overlay. A restored layout is primed, so it is never yanked at boot.
- **Pane editors can no longer be permanently orphaned.** The shared
  per-session Lexical editor used to be reclaimed inside `keydown`/`beforeinput`
  against a 6-repoints/10 s budget, and the guard then stood down forever after
  a few ordinary sidebar switches — the visible pane composer became a plain
  contenteditable (typing painted, Enter/Ctrl+A dead, `/` never opened the
  command menu) while `health()` stayed green. Repairs are now deferred out of
  the keystroke, throttled (one per second) rather than stopped, re-armed once
  stable, and reported through `health().editorRoots`. Ctrl/Cmd+A and the
  last-resort Enter path repair an orphaned host first.
- **`/compact` completion is

dsh-split-screen README · What's new in 1.7.0：Known remaining gap: the compact/TUI composer (Alt+T, or panes shorter than
~280 px) is the plugin's own single-line textarea and still has no native
slash-suggestion menu; type `/` in the full composer (Alt+T) for suggestions.

dsh-split-screen README · Keyboard shortcuts：| Keys | Action |
|------|--------|
| **Alt+T** | Toggle the focused pane between the full composer and the compact TUI line |
| **Alt+Shift+← / → / ↑ / ↓** | Move keyboard focus to the neighboring pane |

Everything else is mouse-driven and works exactly like the stock DeepSeek UI.
On macOS the same chords run with **⌥ Option** in place of Alt (Option+T,
Option+Shift+Arrows).

dsh-split-screen README · What it does：- **Split-only by design** — with a single conversation open you see the
  stock view, untouched: no overlay, no re-hosted composer, nothing covered,
  and every stock control (the workspace chooser, the agent-preset hero on a
  new session) stays clickable. The split workspace appears the moment there
  are two panes and steps aside again when the second-to-last pane closes.
- **Split any pane** — drag a conversation from the DeepSeek sidebar onto a
  pane edge (left / right / top / bottom) to split it there, or drop it in
  the center to swap that pane's conversation. With the split still off,
  dragging a conversation onto the conversation column starts the split: a
  ghost previews the target half, edge drops split in that direction.
- **Native look, light & dark** — panes render with the stock DeepSeek
  styles, theme variables and primitives: user bubbles, Think rows, tool
  rows, the streaming shimmer, the rounded composer card.
- **Fully interactive panes** — every pane is a live session: streaming
  responses, Enter to send, Shift+Enter for newline, /commands, Stop while
  running, queued messages, todos, and image paste & drag-drop a

dsh-split-screen README · Getting started：1. Install the plugin and restart `dsh web` — nothing changes until you
   actually split: one conversation looks and behaves exactly like stock.
2. Drag a conversation from the sidebar onto the conversation column to
   start a split (or drop it on a pane edge once you already have panes).
3. Click a conversation in the sidebar to load it into the focused pane.
4. Use the pane header's split buttons (⬎ / ⬏) for more panes, ✕ to close,
   and drag the dividers between panes to resize. The **?** button (and the
   one-time tip card) lists the shortcuts and how to disable split view.
5. Press **Alt+T** to try the compact TUI composer.

dsh-split-screen README · Safety, recovery and diagnostics (1.7.0)：The plugin is built so that a failing pane can never take the host down with
it. Everything below is available without devtools-only tricks; all state is
reported by one function that returns plain JSON.

**Kill switch** — disables the split workspace unconditionally and persists it
(the saved layout is kept, not deleted):

dsh-split-screen README · Safety, recovery and diagnostics (1.7.0)：**Safe mode (crash-loop guard)** — every deliberate activation is recorded
before it can crash; after the workspace has been up and responsive for ~9 s it
is marked healthy and the crash counter resets. If a previous boot never
reached healthy, or the same guard tripped twice, the next boot does **not**
auto-activate the saved layout:

dsh-split-screen README · Safety, recovery and diagnostics (1.7.0)：- the stock view is untouched and the saved layout is kept,
- a small dismissible chip appears bottom-right:
  *"Split screen paused after a crash — Retry / Disable"*,
- the console gets one actionable warning,
- **Retry** clears the counters and re-activates; **Disable** sets the kill
  switch.

dsh-split-screen README · Safety, recovery and diagnostics (1.7.0)：Repeated render failures (3 boundary catches in ~20 s) also switch to safe mode
automatically, and a workspace-level crash does so immediately. A failing pane
body is isolated with its own *Retry* card — the other panes keep streaming.
A changed plugin release resets the crash guard automatically.

**Diagnostics API** — `window.__dshSplitView`:

dsh-split-screen README · Safety, recovery and diagnostics (1.7.0)：| Method | Returns |
|--------|---------|
| `health()` | `{pluginVersion, hostRelease, testedHost, testedReleases, enabled, safeMode, active, geometryBlocked, panes, maxPanes, blockedReason, failures, lastError, geometry, persistedTree, crashGuard}` |
| `reset()` | clears the saved tree + crash counters, stays in the stock view |
| `retry()` | clears crash counters/safe mode and re-activates the kept tree |
| `help()` | shortcut/help data (the same information as the "?" card) |
| `setEnabled(flag)` | the kill switch |
| `focusChat()`, `closeFocused()` | the companions bridge (`dsh-session-hotkeys`) |

dsh-split-screen README · Safety, recovery and diagnostics (1.7.0)：All methods return plain serializable data and never throw. `health().active`
means "the split workspace is rendered and responsive"; `health().panes` is the
true persisted tree state even while safe mode/geometry keeps it off screen.

dsh-split-screen README · Safety, recovery and diagnostics (1.7.0)：**Tested host versions** — the plugin reads
`window.__DSH_BOOT__?.release?.version` and compares it against a
`TESTED_RELEASES` list (currently `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.2` — the build is
verified on the user's live `0.2.1-rc.2` host). An untested release logs ONE
info note and shows up in `health().testedHost` — activation is never blocked
by the check; the crash loop guard is the protection.

dsh-split-screen README · Safety, recovery and diagnostics (1.7.0)：**Limits** — at most **6** panes (`MAX_PANES`); persisted trees deeper than 6
levels or with duplicate/unknown session ids are repaired or discarded on load.
UI strings are localized (EN/ZH). The split-only contract is unchanged: with
fewer than two panes the plugin renders nothing over the stock UI — its only
chrome is the small fixed chip while safe mode/geometry keeps a saved split
inactive.

dsh-split-screen README · Robustness notes (1.4.0)：- The overlay is constrained to the measured conversation column on **all
  four edges** (sidebar left, details panel right, desktop chrome above and
  below). If the column cannot be measured with confidence on a given shell,
  the workspace **stays inactive** with one console note rather than
  covering a guessed area — the stock UI is never blocked.
- While the split is off, the plugin's steady-state cost is zero: no
  observers, no DOM scraping, no session staging.
- While the split is on, all observation paths are bounded (throttled DOM
  list adapter, settle-and-exit geometry loops, a rate-limited circuit
  breaker on the shared Lexical editor root) so a contested resource fails
  soft instead of freezing the app.
- If the workspace component itself ever throws, it isolates itself: the stock
  view keeps the viewport, the saved layout is kept, and the plugin enters
  **safe mode** with a visible chip (Retry / Disable) instead of disappearing
  silently — see *Safety, recovery and diagnostics* above.

dsh-split-screen README · Agent Teams & mode selector in panes (1.5.0)：- The session header's action row re-hosts completely inside panes: the
  Agent Team trigger, the agent-preset (mode) label, cost-meter statistics
  and every other `conversation.session.header.actions` entry render in both
  the full header (wide panes) and the slim header (narrow panes). The team
  panel itself is portaled above the split overlay, so it is never clipped.
- Clicking a team member in a pane is split-aware: their pane gets focused,
  or their conversation splits in beside the current one (the stock action's
  main-view guard would have ignored the click for pane sessions).
- TUI composer mode keeps its header-less minimal design (Alt+T toggles
  back); with zero or one pane the plugin renders nothing and the stock
  menu bar is untouched.

dsh-split-screen README · Recommended companions：- **[dsh-session-hotkeys](https://github.com/YEYEYEYESHIFU/dsh-session-hotkeys)** —
  keyboard-first control for the DeepSeek Harness: `Esc` returns focus to the
  conversation, `Alt+Enter` steers or queues while an agent runs, the model
  picker is keyboard-reachable, and every shortcut is rebindable in a visual
  panel. Works great inside split-screen panes.
- **[dsh-result-only-view](https://github.com/YEYEYEYESHIFU/dsh-result-only-view)** —
  a compact results-only reading mode for running sessions: less visual
  noise while several agents work side by side in your panes.

dsh-split-screen README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-split-screen
```

then restart `dsh web`.

dsh-split-screen README · How it works：- Client-only plugin: the host half is an empty loader entry; everything
  runs in the browser on public service surfaces (`sessions`, `slots`,
  `conversation`), plus a small per-session staging bridge (`session.open()`).
- Panes stage real sessions through the sessions service (history window +
  live event stream), so every pane is a first-class conversation.
- Injects: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout` (owner of the `shell.overlay`
  slot the workspace mounts into), `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale`,
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`.
- The stock DeepSeek sidebar is deliberately untouched — it stays the single
  source of truth for conversations.
- Transcripts reuse the ui-conversation CSS module rules (copied verbatim
  under `dsv-` class names) so a harness upgrade cannot silently break
  the look.

dsh-split-screen README · Development / tests：No dependencies and no build step: `lib/client.js` is the shipped browser
bundle, written for `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})`, and is
syntax-checked directly. Node.js 18+ runs the suites (CI uses Node 24).

```bash
node --check lib/client.js   # bundle syntax
npm test                     # both sandboxed suites (smoke + safety)
```

dsh-split-screen README · Development / tests：- `tests/smoke.mjs` (16 assertions) evaluates the bundle under a stub DOM and
  covers the module-loader contract, the double-apply guard, the global-chord /
  drag-bridge / IME listener lifetimes, full teardown + re-apply, and the
  split-only activation gate for empty, single-pane and two-pane persisted
  trees.
- `tests/safety.mjs` (117 assertions) covers the 1.6.0–1.7.0 hardening:
  0.2.0/0.2.1 frame-geometry fixtures (`shell.bottom`/handles/overlay excluded,

a DSH profile and never start or contact the running app. CI runs the same

dsh-split-screen README · Compatibility：- Requires **DSH 0.1.5 or newer**. Verified end-to-end on Windows against
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-rc.2` and on `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2` under
  `dsh web` and the 0.2.0 desktop composition (same client, desktop profile
  bundles + patch layer). `TESTED_RELEASES` in the bundle lists the releases
  the build is signed off against; `health().testedHost` reports the live
  comparison.
- **0.2.1 support (1.6.0)** — the 0.2.1 shell and renderer differ in two ways
  the 1.5.x line could not survive: the frame gained a static `shell.bottom`
  row (which broke the conversation-column measurement, making split view a
  silent no-op) and content moved to a new factory-slot render dispatcher
  (`renderFactorySlot`) that every user bubble and the model label call. 1.6.0
  fixes both: the geometry is now selected structurally (center column +
  validated grid-track fallback, `shell.bottom`/handles/overlay excluded), and
  panes receive a guarded `renderFactorySlot` outlet plus the
  declared-children `renderSlot`/`renderSlotChain` seats the stock renderer
  attaches. The live `0.2.1-rc.2` host is **verified** on the isolated real
  0.2.1 desktop host
